findings.desc: quality-cleanup: declared-artifact-commit-check.ts:78-87 classifyDeclaredArtifactCommitState checks `ignored` before `tracked`, which misclassifies a committed-but-gitignored file as `git-ignored` (blocking) instead of `committed-clean` (passing). In git a file committed before .gitignore was updated remains tracked; `tracked=true, ignored=true` is a valid real state. The comment at line 78 says `a git-ignored path can never be committed` which is incorrect. Fix: move the `tracked && !dirty` check before the `ignored` check so a committed clean file passes regardless of gitignore status.

quality-cleanup: dirty-worktree.ts:188-197 classifyDeclarablePath does not check `findRuntimeArtifactEntry`, so `artifact_declare` accepts runtime artifact paths (e.g. `.koala-serve.json`) without error. At dirty-check time the classifier correctly classifies them as `runtime_artifact_changes` (not `declared_artifact_changes`), so the declaration is silently ineffective but not a security bypass. However the fail-fast UX contract (`assertDeclarablePath`) is violated: declaring a runtime artifact path succeeds but produces no useful effect. The `NonDeclarableCategory` type does not include `runtime_artifact_changes`, and the comment in the docstring says `classifyDeclarablePath` reuses the EXACT classifier vocabulary — but it skips the runtime artifact check. Low-severity correctness gap.
